Accused no.1 in S.C.No.73/2020 pending before the Court of III Addl. District & Sessions Judge,
Hassan, arising out of Crime No.191/2019 registered by Holenarasipura Town Police Station,
Hassan District, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 302 IPC and Sections 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, is before this Court under Section 439 Cr.PC.

sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned Counsel for the parties.

3. FIR in Crime No.191/2019 was registered by Holenarasipura Town Police for the offence punishable under Section 302 IPC against the petitioner herein on the basis of the complaint lodged by Rakesha.H.S., S/o late Swamy who is the brother of deceased Kavya who was married to the petitioner on 22.07.2012.

Kavya was found dead in her matrimonial house in a suspicious manner and complainant suspected the hand of the petitioner in the death of his sister, and therefore, he had approached the police and lodged the complaint, which had resulted in registering the FIR against the petitioner.
During the course of investigation of the case, petitioner was arrested on 10.12.2019.
His bail application filed before the Trial Court in S.C.No.73/2020 was rejected on 04.10.2023.
Therefore, he is before this Court.
5. Learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioner is in custody for more than four years.
The trial of the case is not likely to be completed in the near soon.
Out of 41 charge sheet witnesses only one charge sheet witness has been partially examined till date.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
6. Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the petition.
7. The material on record would go to show that the petitioner's earlier bail application was dismissed by the learned Sessions Judge on merits by order dated 12.01.2021.
Thereafter, the second bail application was filed by the petitioner on the ground of delay in trial.
The prosecution has cited totally 41 charge sheet witnesses in the present case.

In the month of May 2020, the case Mr Shankara vs State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165653613/
2 was committed to the jurisdictional Sessions Court and on 15.06.2020 case was NC:
2023:KHC:45099 registered before the jurisdictional Sessions Court in S.C.No.73/2020.
8.

entities.text: Mr Shankara vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: From a perusal of the order sheet of the Trial Court, it is seen that charges were framed against the petitioner by the Trial Court on 08.03.2021 and summons was issued to the charge sheet witnesses on 19.08.2021.
Examination of CW-1 as PW-1 was commenced on 22.12.2021.

Till date,
the examination of PW-1 is not complete.
The order sheet maintained by the Trial Court would go to show that on most of the dates, the accused was not produced before the Court and on some of the dates, PW-1 was not present.
The matter was also adjourned at the request of the accused to enable him to engage the services of an advocate.
From a perusal of the order sheet, it is seen that the learned Sessions Judge has not made satisfactory efforts for expediting the trial even though the accused is in custody.

Though bail application was filed before the Sessions Court on the ground of delay in trial and long incarceration of the petitioner in jail, the learned Sessions Judge has failed to appreciate the grounds put forward by the petitioner for grant of bail.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of ANGELA HARISH SONTAKKE VS STATE OF MAHARASHTRA - (2021)3 SCC 723, wherein the accused persons were charged for the offences under the provisions of Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, having considered the seriousness of the charges and the period of custody suffered by the accused, had granted bail to the accused notwithstanding the rigor under Section 43- D(5) of the said Act considering the fact that the accused had suffered five years incarceration.

entities.text: ANGELA HARISH SONTAKKE VS STATE OF MAHARASHTRA - (2021)3 SCC 723
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. In the case of SAGAR TATYARAM GORKHE VS STATE OF MAHARASHTRA - (2021)3 SCC 725, considering the fact that the accused persons were in jail for a period of four years, and there were 147 witnesses who were still to be examined, the Hon'ble Supreme Court had enlarged the accused on bail.

entities.text: SAGAR TATYARAM GORKHE VS STATE OF MAHARASHTRA - (2021)3 SCC 725
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. In the case of UNION OF INDIA VS K.A.NAJEEB - (2021)3 SCC 713, considering the fact that the accused were in jail for a period of more than five years and there were 276 witnesses left to be examined, the Hon'ble Supreme Court had refused to interfere with the order granting bail to the accused by the High Court on the ground of delay in trial and long period of incarceration suffered by the accused.

entities.text: UNION OF INDIA VS K.A.NAJEEB - (2021)3 SCC 713
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, the petitioner is in custody from 10.12.2019.
As on this date, he is in custody for more than four years.

Considering the fact that after commencement of trial in the last more than two years only one witness has been partially examined by the Trial Court, it can be safely assumed that the trial of the case is not likely to be completed in the near soon.

Under the circumstances, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the view that the petitioner's bail application is required to be allowed only on the ground of delay in trial and prolonged period of incarceration of the petitioner in jail.

Accordingly, the following order:
Mr Shankara vs State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165653613/
3 13.
The petition is allowed.
